claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a random distribution of constituent atoms.
Controlled thermal annealing can increase short-range atomic ordering in the PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst.
Annealing can increase ordering while preserving overall composition and nanoparticle size.
Surface short-range atomic order governs ethanol-oxidation activity and selectivity.
Increasing short-range order creates more favorable binding configurations for ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Enhanced atomic ordering stabilizes specific surface configurations.
The ordered surface configurations optimize the adsorption energies of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Adsorption-energy tuning reduces unwanted over-oxidation and side reactions.
Reduced over-oxidation and side reactions improve catalytic activity and product selectivity.
Relative to the as-synthesized catalyst, an annealed catalyst with greater short-range order will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current density.
Relative to the as-synthesized catalyst, an annealed catalyst with greater short-range order will show increased selectivity toward acetaldehyde over CO2.
The predicted ordering effect applies only when annealing does not cause significant sintering, phase segregation, or morphological change.
The predicted ordering effect applies within typical ethanol-oxidation potential and temperature ranges.
A lack of statistically significant activity improvement or selectivity change after a confirmed increase in ordering would falsify the hypothesis.
Performance improvement without a corresponding change in atomic ordering would falsify the proposed ordering-based explanation.
